newsitem.title: UK: British Gas rejects Ofgas TransCo price controls.
newsitem.headline: British Gas rejects Ofgas TransCo price controls.

text.p: British Gas Plc said on Thursday that it has rejected price controls proposed by UK gas industry regulator Ofgas for its transmission and pipeline business, TransCo.
British Gas said in a statement that the proposals were "unjustified and unworkable."

The rejection means that the senior British competition authority, the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) will be asked to conduct an inquiry into the proposals which could take many months to complete.
British Gas chairman Richard Giordano said in a statement that it was regrettable that efforts to achieve an acceptable resolution had failed.
"The MMC, which thoroughly considered the whole issue in 1992/93, is being asked to look at it again," he said.

British Gas deputy chairman Philip Rogerson, who is in charge of regulatory issues for the group, said Ofgas' original proposals made in May were damaging to British Gas shareholders' interests and "not in the overall interests of gas consumers."
He said concessions made by Ofgas in August remained "unrealistic and unacceptable."
Ofgas proposed that TransCo cut charges to gas suppliers by 20 percent in 1997 and then by 6.5 percent below inflation for four years.
British Gas said the controls would not allow it enough money to invest adequately in its infrastructure.
